topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic opens the lecture by connecting to histopathology practicals and setting out the learning outcomes.

topics.label: Tumor viruses, proto-oncogenes, and transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the study of infectious tumor viruses revealed cellular proto-oncogenes and led to laboratory assays for measuring cellular transformation.

topics.label: Classification and genetic mechanisms of oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the functional categories of cancer-associated genes and illustrate their genetic mechanisms and effects on cell cycle regulation.

topics.label: Mechanisms and manifestations of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the causes and cellular consequences of sequence and chromosomal instability, focusing on defects in DNA repair, replication, and mitosis.

topics.label: Multi-step tumor progression, hereditary predisposition, and tumor evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how sequential mutation accumulation drives tumor development in sporadic and hereditary cancers and affects tumor evolution.

topics.label: Conclusion and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture with summary remarks, a book recommendation, and a preview of the next lecture topic.
